strengths: Conditional bins (konbini customer vs machine vs home) match how locals actually read street space
Carry-home friction is admitted—complaints, sticky wrappers, tourist bags—not only ideal manners
Generational split on 1995 memory vs bin scarcity as 'normal' feels locally true

issues.problem: Labeling the habit **mochikaeri** presents takeout jargon as if it were the everyday name for carrying trash home. Locals say ゴミを持って帰る; 持ち帰り usually means takeaway food.
issues.suggestion: Drop mochikaeri as a trash-habit label; describe carrying waste home in plain English, optionally noting takeaway packaging as a separate mochikaeri (持ち帰り) context.

issues.location: ## Litter Still Exists — Keep the Picture Honest
issues.problem: 'Many Japanese people take pride in not littering' edges toward national character talk even though the next sentences balance it.
issues.suggestion: Anchor in practice: 'Many people treat street litter as a personal failure of manners' rather than pride as a national trait.
